_intro_template: {title}. What you see is a map of {total} electrosurgical and advanced energy devices from the FDA's device registry — organized into {n_clusters} clusters. Curvo's language model read every product description and grouped them by the meaning it found. The largest regions are {top1}, {top2}, and {top3}. Let's explore.
_outro: And that completes our tour of the electrosurgical landscape. From simple bipolar forceps to advanced energy platforms, this map reveals how energy-based surgical devices cluster by function and design. What Curvo has built is not a human-defined taxonomy — it's a map of relationships discovered by reading how these devices describe themselves. This is what Curvo can do with any product catalogue.
Electrosurgery Tools: Electrosurgery Tools. This is the largest cluster, with over a thousand devices spanning generators, handpieces, footswitches, pencils, and return electrodes. Together they form the core infrastructure of every electrosurgical theatre.
Bipolar Forceps: Bipolar Forceps. Over a thousand instruments crafted for precise haemostasis. These paired-electrode devices let surgeons coagulate tissue with pinpoint control, ranging from fine microsurgical tips to robust general-purpose designs.
Bayonet Bipolar Forceps: Bayonet Bipolar Forceps. Nearly a thousand instruments with the distinctive offset bayonet profile that keeps the surgeon's hand clear of the operative field. These are workhorses of neurosurgery and skull base procedures.
Bayonet Bipolar Forceps_2: Bayonet Bipolar Forceps. A second, smaller collection of around five hundred bayonet-style forceps. These tend toward longer shaft lengths and finer tip configurations for deeper surgical access.
Piezoelectric Surgical Tools: Piezoelectric Surgical Tools. Close to a thousand devices that use ultrasonic vibration rather than heat to cut bone. From dental piezosurgery inserts to orthopaedic osteotomes, they offer precise bone work with minimal soft tissue damage.
Electrosurgical Tools: Electrosurgical Tools. Over eight hundred devices including monopolar pencils, blade electrodes, and suction coagulators. These are the everyday cutting and coagulation instruments found in virtually every operating room.
Ophthalmic Surgical Tools: Ophthalmic Surgical Tools. Around eight hundred instruments adapted for eye surgery. Many feature monopolar and bipolar configurations with ultra-fine tips designed for the delicate anatomy of orbital and periorbital procedures.
Radiofrequency Surgical Tools: Radiofrequency Surgical Tools. Over six hundred devices that deliver targeted RF energy for tissue ablation and pain management. This cluster includes RF needles, probes, and generators used in spine, cardiac, and aesthetic procedures.
Laparoscopic Grasping Forceps: Laparoscopic Grasping Forceps. Around four hundred instruments built for minimally invasive abdominal surgery. Maryland dissectors, Babcock graspers, and biopsy cups — all designed to work through five-millimetre ports.
Reusable Bipolar Forceps: Reusable Bipolar Forceps. Nearly four hundred autoclavable bipolar instruments. These durable forceps are designed for hundreds of sterilisation cycles, offering both economic and environmental advantages over disposable alternatives.
Bipolar Surgical Cables: Bipolar Surgical Cables. Around three hundred and forty cables, cords, and connectors that link bipolar instruments to their generators. Silicone-insulated and available in various pin configurations to match different manufacturer systems.
Mariner Surgical Implants: Mariner Surgical Implants. Over three hundred pedicle screws, rods, and fixation hardware from the Mariner spinal system. These titanium and cobalt-chrome components form a modular posterior fixation platform.
Mariner Orthopaedic Implants: Mariner Orthopaedic Implants. Around two hundred and seventy devices including joint replacement components and fracture fixation hardware. This cluster extends the Mariner product line beyond the spine into hip and trauma applications.
MicroFrance Forceps: MicroFrance Forceps. About two hundred and forty instruments from this specialist manufacturer. Known for their fine-tipped designs and ergonomic handles, these forceps serve microsurgical and ENT procedures.
Bipolar Surgical Instrumentation: Bipolar Surgical Instrumentation. Around two hundred and forty devices that combine bipolar energy delivery with specialised instrument profiles. These span multiple surgical disciplines and manufacturer lines.
Spine Implants: Spine Implants. Just over two hundred cortical screws, taps, and bone probes. These are the ancillary components that support spinal fusion procedures alongside the larger rod and screw systems.
Bayonet Forceps: Bayonet Forceps. About a hundred and seventy non-insulated bayonet forceps, primarily in stainless steel and titanium. These simpler designs serve as general-purpose tissue handling instruments.
Reusable Surgical Forceps: Reusable Surgical Forceps. Around a hundred and fifty autoclavable instruments spanning both monopolar and bipolar designs. These durable forceps are built for repeated sterilisation and long service life.
Malis Bipolar Forceps: Malis Bipolar Forceps. About a hundred and twenty instruments bearing the Malis name, a standard in neurosurgical coagulation since the nineteen sixties. Available in both insulated and non-stick variants with tip sizes from point three to two millimetres.
CLARIS Bipolar Forceps: CLARIS Bipolar Forceps. Around ninety instruments from Bissinger's premium CLARIS line. These German-engineered non-stick forceps feature the distinctive keyhole bayonet profile and are available in both flat-plug and two-pin configurations.
Malis Forceps: Malis Forceps. A collection of about eighty classic Malis-pattern bipolar forceps with non-stick tips. These deliver current with exceptional accuracy for safe cauterisation of delicate neural tissue.
Malis Forceps_2: Malis Forceps. A smaller group of about sixty Malis-style instruments, primarily in titanium with irrigation capability. The irrigating feature helps prevent tissue adherence during prolonged coagulation.
DORO Forceps: DORO Forceps. Sixty instruments from this specialist line of non-stick bipolar forceps. Available in straight and bayonet keyhole profiles, the DORO range spans ten to twenty-five centimetre lengths with tips as fine as point four millimetres.
Bipolar Forceps Variety: Bipolar Forceps Variety. Over fourteen hundred instruments representing the broadest cross-section of bipolar forceps designs. From Adson patterns to DeBakey profiles, this cluster captures the full diversity of two-electrode coagulation instruments.
Electrosurgical Instruments: Electrosurgical Instruments. Over eleven hundred devices including generators, pencils, and active electrodes. These form the core energy delivery platform for modern surgery, converting electrical current into precise tissue effects.
Minimally Invasive Surgical: Minimally Invasive Surgical. Over seven hundred devices designed for keyhole procedures. Insulated shafts, rotating handles, and modular inserts allow surgeons to cut, grasp, and coagulate through small port incisions.
Surgical Forceps: Surgical Forceps. Over six hundred general-purpose forceps spanning both monopolar and bipolar configurations. This cluster captures the everyday tissue-handling instruments found across all surgical specialties.
Spinal Fixation Hardware: Spinal Fixation Hardware. Around three hundred and thirty screws, plates, and connecting rods. These implantable components provide the mechanical stability needed for spinal fusion and deformity correction.
Surgical Scissors: Surgical Scissors. Over three hundred powered and electrosurgical cutting instruments. Unlike traditional scissors, many in this group use bipolar or ultrasonic energy to simultaneously cut and seal tissue.
Electrosurgical Cables: Electrosurgical Cables. Nearly three hundred cables and adapters connecting instruments to generator units. Available in reusable and single-use configurations with various connector standards.
Spinal Surgical Instrumentation: Spinal Surgical Instrumentation. Around two hundred and seventy surgical tools used during spinal procedures. Screwdrivers, reduction instruments, and rod holders that surgeons use to place and adjust spinal implants.
Ultrasonic Scalers: Ultrasonic Scalers. About two hundred and sixty devices that use high-frequency vibration for dental and surgical scaling. These range from handheld dental units to sophisticated surgical dissectors.
Minimally Invasive Surgery: Minimally Invasive Surgery. Around two hundred and forty devices including trocars, insufflation accessories, and port-access instruments. These enable the keyhole approach that reduces patient recovery time.
Laparoscopic Forceps: Laparoscopic Forceps. About two hundred and forty instruments specifically designed for abdominal keyhole surgery. Maryland dissectors and grasping forceps predominate, most with five-millimetre shaft diameters.
Cortical Shanks: Cortical Shanks. Around two hundred and thirty specialised screw shanks from the Mariner system. These cortical-engaging components come in solid and cannulated variants for different vertebral bone densities.
Mariner Rod System: Mariner Rod System. About two hundred and twenty rods, connectors, and reduction tools from the Mariner spinal platform. Straight and pre-contoured rods in cobalt-chrome and titanium provide the longitudinal framework for spinal constructs.
Aesthetic Surgical Tools: Aesthetic Surgical Tools. Around two hundred and twenty devices used in cosmetic and reconstructive procedures. This cluster includes RF skin tightening probes, liposuction cannulae, and energy-based tissue remodelling instruments.
Endoscopic Electrosurgery: Endoscopic Electrosurgery. About two hundred and fifteen devices that combine endoscopic visualisation with electrosurgical energy delivery. Resectoscope loops, roller-ball electrodes, and flexible probe tips serve urological and gynaecological procedures.
Cushing Forceps Tools: Cushing Forceps Tools. Around two hundred instruments in the Cushing pattern, characterised by straight shafts and serrated tips. Originally designed for neurosurgery, these versatile forceps now serve multiple specialties.
Medical Cables & Leads: Medical Cables and Leads. About a hundred and ninety specialised cables connecting surgical instruments to their power sources. These include patient return electrodes, bipolar cords, and generator interface cables.
Surgical Instrumentation: Surgical Instrumentation. Around a hundred and seventy miscellaneous surgical instruments that span multiple energy modalities. This cluster captures devices that don't fit neatly into a single forceps or electrode category.
Ultrasonic Medical Tools: Ultrasonic Medical Tools. About a hundred and seventy devices that harness ultrasonic energy for cutting and coagulation. Advanced harmonic scalpels and cavitational ultrasonic aspirators sit alongside simpler dental instruments.
Bipolar Forceps Inserts: Bipolar Forceps Inserts. Around a hundred and sixty modular insert tips for bipolar forceps systems. These interchangeable components allow surgeons to swap tip profiles without replacing the entire instrument.
Endoscopic Surgical: Endoscopic Surgical. About a hundred and sixty devices for endoscopic procedures. Flexible and rigid instruments that combine visualisation with tissue manipulation inside body cavities.
Electrode Accessories: Electrode Accessories. Around a hundred and fifty adapters, holders, and disposable tips that support electrosurgical electrodes. These consumable components ensure reliable electrical contact and sterile delivery.
Ultrasonic Surgical Tools: Ultrasonic Surgical Tools. About a hundred and forty instruments using focused ultrasonic vibration for bone cutting and tissue dissection. Piezosurgery handpieces and dedicated tip sets predominate in this group.
Robotic Surgical Tools: Robotic Surgical Tools. Around a hundred and forty instruments designed for robotic-assisted surgery platforms. These feature specialised wrist articulations and insulated shafts compatible with robotic arm interfaces.
